data.name: Marzug
data.gender_notes: Marzug is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic word 'Murzugh', meaning 'a strong, steadfast, or brave camel'. This name evokes images of strength, courage, and power, making it an excellent choice for a baby boy. The name Marzug carries the meaning “Steadfast, Brave” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Marzug usually hope their child will grow to embody steadfast, brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Marzug is a name that represents the inner strength and courage that we all possess. It reminds us to stand firm in our beliefs and to face challenges with bravery and determination.
data.etymology: Marzug belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Steadfast, Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marzug total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_urdu.name: مرزوق
in_urdu.meaning: بارش کا مالک، نیکو قسم کا مالک، نیکو قسم کا وارث، اچھا قسم کا مالک
in_urdu.long_meaning: مرزوق کا نام اچھی قسم کا مالک ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کہ اللہ تعالیٰ نے اسے اپنے فضل سے نیکو قسم کا مالک بنایا ہے، اور اللہ تعالیٰ نے اپنے فضل سے اسے نیکو قسم کا وارث بھی بنایا ہے۔ یہ نام اس کی بھلائی اور خوش قسمتی کا اشارہ ہے، اور اس کے نیک کردار اور نیک کاموں کا بھی اشارہ ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मरज़ुक़

in_hindi.long_meaning: मरज़ुक़ का नाम अच्छी किस्मत का मालिक है, जिसका अर्थ है कि अल्लाह ने इसे अपनी कृपा से अच्छी किस्मत का मालिक बनाया है, और अल्लाह ने अपनी कृपा से इसे अच्छी किस्मत का वारिस भी बनाया है। यह नाम अच्छी किस्मत और समृद्धि का प्रतीक है, और इसके अच्छे व्यक्तित्व और अच्छे कामों का भी प्रतीक है।

historical_references.reference: Marzug was the name of a place in the Sassanid Empire, mentioned in the Arabic historical text Kitab al-Aghani by Ibn al-Farid al-Sirafi. It was a town in the province of Adharbayjan, known for its wine production and fine horses. Marzug was also the site of a famous annual horse race, attended by nobles and dignitaries.

The name Marzug is also mentioned in the works of Persian poet Farrokhzad who wrote in the 16th century CE about the ancient ruins of the city. She described Marzug as a once prosperous and cultured city that had been reduced to ruins, and expressed a sense of longing for its past glory.
